title: Rest circles, with airport stakes back on market
full_text:
Perth Airport is once again in the crosshairs of infrastructure buyers, with shareholders reviving a sale process for their stakes in the $6bn-plus infrastructure asset.
Sources say Rest Superannuation, which owns a stake in Moorabbin Airport, could be circling.
Established in 1988, Rest is one of Australia’s largest profit-to-member superannuation funds, with more than 2 million members and about $112bn in funds under management as at June 30.
DataRoom understands that Macquarie-controlled entity The Infrastructure Fund and Australian Retirement Trust are both again attempting to find a buyer for their holdings in Perth Airport through investment bank UBS.
The pair own 9.14 per cent of the airport combined, and a deal could result in an infrastructure investor gaining control of the holding for at least $600m.
The same investors made efforts to sell their holdings in Perth Airport in 2023, after existing investors passed up the opportunity to increase their holding.
Sources said at the time that they were looking at a price of about 27 times earnings, a price at the time that could value the asset more highly than Sydney or Melbourne airports.
Some buyers in the market two years ago took a view that the real price was about a third less.
Other shareholders in Perth Airport are Utilities Trust of Australia (40.6 per cent), Future Fund (30.01 per cent) and AustralianSuper (20.25 per cent), while TIF owns 7.19 per cent and ART 1.95 per cent.
Perth Airport is the fourth-busiest airport in Australia for passenger traffic. For the 2025-26 financial year it recorded 18.39 million passengers, up from 17.48 million a year earlier, as buoyant mining activity in Western Australia fuels passenger demand.
Rest is sizing up Perth Airport after several airport stakes have been on offer over the past two years. The super fund also has exposure to Melbourne Airport, which has been at the centre of a high-profile legal battle involving Dexus and a secretive attempt to offload a 10 per cent stake, dubbed Project Mercury.
It was discovered by co-owners IFM Investors, the Future Fund and others and the NSW Supreme Court found Dexus failed to act openly and honestly.
The NSW Supreme Court ruling validated a default notice that could ultimately force Dexus to sell its stake in Australia Pacific Airports Corporation.
The expectation is that the Dexus wholesale investor interests that own the airport stake ultimately will sell it to IFM and UTA in the coming months as a result, but this could be at a loss.
An acquisition for IFM would come just months after it acquired more than 67 per cent of Atlas Arteria following its hostile bid valuing the listed toll-road operator at $7.4bn.
Several high-profile private wealth businesses have exposure to the Dexus wholesale fund that owns Melbourne Airport. The airport is owned by Australian Pacific Airports Corp, which also owns Launceston Airport.
APAC investors include Dexus funds with 27.3 per cent, the Morrison-managed UTA fund (8.7 per cent), IFM (25.17 per cent), the Future Fund (20.34 per cent) and TCorp (18.47 per cent).
Other airport deals include KKR and Skip Capital buying a 74.25 per cent stake in Gold Coast Airport owner Queensland Airports Ltd for about $3bn in 2024. North Queensland Airports, which owns Cairns and Mackay airports, was on the market last year but existing shareholder JPMorgan Asset Management bought out the remaining stake and ultimately took full control.
